name: semaphore-arm-tension
title: Semaphore Arm Tension
description: A status control drawn as a UK lower-quadrant mechanical semaphore: gravity holds the arm at Danger, and it only reaches Clear when the signal wire is under tension — position is the only state carrier, no coloured aspect glass. The arm and counterweight breathe on a slow wire-tension bob and the lamp flickers like a real flame, both independent of whichever state it's holding.
useWhen: a binary status/gate needs to read as physically fail-safe rather than as a coloured badge — the arm's own angle is the only signal, so a viewer reads Danger/Clear from position and never from hue, and the constant wire-tension bob plus lamp flicker keep it alive at rest with zero input; pick switch-eclipse instead for a general-purpose on/off toggle with no status-honesty narrative, or status-sphere-dots when the states are process cadences (thinking/searching/done) rather than a two-value gate.
instruction: A status control rendered as a UK lower-quadrant mechanical semaphore signal: a post with a pivoting arm at its top, a counterweight hanging below on a short link, and a fixed-luminance lamp housing behind the pivot. `cleared` (boolean, controlled) / `defaultCleared` (uncontrolled, default false) drives the arm's resting rotation — 0deg (horizontal) for Danger, 55deg (rotated toward the track) for Clear — and that angle is the ONLY carrier of state; the lamp is never tinted red or green, it only ever changes luminance. Two independent continuous motions run on a single requestAnimationFrame loop that writes directly to SVG element attributes via refs (no React re-render per frame, no CSS transition on the rotate attribute since the same attribute is already being written every frame): a 9-second sinusoidal 'wire tension' bob nudges the arm's rotation ±2.2deg around its current resting angle and rocks the counterweight ±4px vertically in the opposite phase, standing in for a real signal wire's continuous give under thermal length change; and a lamp glow opacity sampled at 12Hz from a seeded PRNG (mulberry32) and linearly interpolated between samples, ranging 0.82-1.0, standing in for a real oil flame's slow candle-like flicker rather than a strobe. A discrete click, Enter, or Space toggles `cleared` and animates the resting angle itself from its previous value to the new target with a hand-computed back-ease overshoot (the same cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1) family used elsewhere in the registry, computed per-frame here because it has to compose with the same rotate attribute the ambient bob is writing) over 650ms. Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, the whole rAF loop stops — no bob, no flicker, no overshoot, a toggle becomes an instant angle change — but this NEVER overrides which state the arm is actually displaying; a live Danger status stays visibly Danger under reduced motion, the demo's own default state (`defaultCleared`) is what determines the resting frame reduced-motion users see. `interactive` (default true) renders a `role=switch` button with `aria-checked` reflecting `cleared`, an `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` pair naming the current Danger/Clear state in a screen-reader description, and a `focus-visible` ring in `--ns-accent` (the only place accent chrome appears — never on the arm, lamp, or counterweight); passing `interactive={false}` renders a read-only `role=status` display for a pure indicator use. Every ink is a Tailwind token class (`text-foreground`/`text-ns-muted`/`text-border`/`text-background`) painted via `fill-current`/`stroke-current`, so both themes repaint for free with zero JS colour reads. Geometry is a fixed 200x240 SVG viewBox rendered at `w-full h-[240px]`, so it scales uniformly to the card. Props: `cleared`, `defaultCleared`, `onClearedChange`, `label` (default 'Signal'), `interactive`, `aria-label` override, `className`. Zero dependencies, DOM+SVG+CSS only, no canvas.
